intro: The Ovarian Tumour — Toronto / FIGO Stage is a oncology scoring tool used in paediatric practice. Paediatric ovarian (usually germ-cell) tumour staging. It scores 1 criteria and interprets the total across 4 bands, so the number always arrives with the severity it implies rather than on its own. In PediAid each criterion is shown as a labelled option with the weight it carries, so the total can be checked rather than taken on trust.
indications: Grading severity at the bedside in oncology
Recording an objective severity band in the case notes
Deciding when a total crosses the threshold for escalation
Re-scoring to track whether a child is improving or deteriorating
Checking the exact criteria of a score used infrequently
method: The score sums 1 criteria: Extent of disease. Totals are then banded: 1 stage or more - Stage I: stage I - surgery alone with surveillance is often sufficient for germ-cell tumours; excellent prognosis; 2 stage or more - Stage II: stage II - surgery plus platinum-based chemotherapy; 3 stage or more - Stage III: stage III - surgery plus chemotherapy; monitor tumour markers (AFP, β-hCG) for response; 4 stage or more - Stage IV: stage IV - distant metastases. Platinum-based chemotherapy; germ-cell tumours remain highly curable even at this stage.
guidelineRefs: Source: Gupta S, Aitken JF, Bartels U et al. Paediatric cancer stage in population-based cancer registries: the Toronto consensus principles and guidelines. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:e163-72.

faqs.q: How many criteria does the Ovarian Tumour — Toronto / FIGO Stage use?
What do the bands of the Ovarian Tumour — Toronto / FIGO Stage mean?
faqs.a: The total is interpreted as: 1 stage or more - Stage I: stage I - surgery alone with surveillance is often sufficient for germ-cell tumours; excellent prognosis; 2 stage or more - Stage II: stage II - surgery plus platinum-based chemotherapy; 3 stage or more - Stage III: stage III - surgery plus chemotherapy; monitor tumour markers (AFP, β-hCG) for response; 4 stage or more - Stage IV: stage IV - distant metastases. Platinum-based chemotherapy; germ-cell tumours remain highly curable even at this stage.

faqs.q: Does the score replace clinical judgement?
faqs.a: No. It is a structured way to record and communicate severity. A clinician concerned about a child should act on that concern regardless of the total.

faqs.q: Where does this score come from?
faqs.a: Source: Gupta S, Aitken JF, Bartels U et al. Paediatric cancer stage in population-based cancer registries: the Toronto consensus principles and guidelines. Lancet Oncol 2016;17:e163-72.
